nodes.description: The initiating lesion is a heterozygous germline FHOD3 variant. Most reported disease alleles are non-truncating - missense, in-frame indels, canonical splice-site variants predicted to skip in-frame cardiac exons, and in-frame deletions of exons 15-16 - and they cluster in a conserved coiled-coil segment (amino acids 622-655), the diaphanous inhibitory domain and the cardiac-specific exon 12. The genetic association itself is established; what the alleles do to the protein is not. The clustering and the absence of a phenotype in Fhod3 heterozygous mice argue against simple haploinsufficiency, but no patient allele has been tested biochemically, so the functional impact is recorded as UNKNOWN rather than as dominant negative.

nodes.description: The heart-enriched long isoform FHOD3L nucleates actin and elongates filaments, and its elongation activity specifically is required for sarcomere formation and contraction. Its sarcomeric position depends on the cardiac-specific N-terminal region, which binds cardiac myosin-binding protein C and directs FHOD3 to the C-zone of the A-band; myofibril targeting is also regulated by CK2 phosphorylation of a muscle-specific exon. Disease alleles are predicted to disturb this localised actin assembly, either by reducing activity or by mislocalising it, but which of these happens for patient alleles is unknown. All evidence for this node is from cell-culture and animal systems.
